comparisonBar: Coursera learner experience: clear hierarchy, low-friction continuation, useful feedback, and trustworthy progress states.

currentComparison.target: Synau learner workspace vs public Coursera course information architecture
currentComparison.result: Synau now has a persistent course rail, a flowing single-column article lesson, explicit progress state, Google-only authentication with first-login profile completion, low-stakes repeatable quizzes, a focused roadmap approval step, a provider-first backend configuration, a visible credit wallet with four transparent top-up packages, and a learning-path manager. New lessons are genuinely on-demand after roadmap approval and render one natural article with a key takeaway and references. Paragraph is the default; code, KaTeX equation, Mermaid diagram, structured table, and quote are optional inline blocks validated by Zod and rendered by explicit UI components. The lesson prompt now requires a distinct editorial opening, avoids overview duplication, selects diagrams for structural ideas, and preserves the learner's language. Active quiz generation is exactly three questions: two article-grounded and one challenge. All fixed Sumopod generator calls use the non-streaming tool path, reserve exactly one credit, charge only after valid completion, return failed/stale reservations, and record input, cached input, output, total tokens, and credit cost. The latest performance pass adds metadata-first Supabase read models, transactional CRUD RPCs, targeted client caching, and request-level timing evidence.
currentComparison.evidence: Live captures: quality/dashboard-final.png, quality/product-brief-final.png, quality/credits-final.png, quality/ui-shell-final.png, quality/tema-provider-roadmap.png, quality/e2e-final.png, quality/tema-provider-e2e.png, quality/prompt-personal-branding.png; reference capture: quality/coursera-course.png.

biggestGap: Core CRUD now stays within one Supabase operation query, but shared Data API/network variance remains visible in remote round trips (roughly 0.13–0.68s in the latest probe); optional renderer chunks over 500 kB remain route-scoped. Hosted Supabase Google provider credentials and exact Auth redirect URLs still need dashboard setup, while Midtrans credentials remain a separate paid top-up blocker.

latestResults.result: Roadmap, article lesson, grounded three-question quiz, public quiz, internal quiz, auth, course, progress, credits, top-up, and Midtrans notification payloads have Zod schemas with semantic validation. Lesson content is limited to paragraph, code, equation, Mermaid, table, and quote blocks.

Public quizzes hide answer keys; duplicate lesson opens collapse to one generation; repeated attempts cannot rewrite history; fixed provider credentials stay server-side; credit holds cannot make a wallet negative.

Live browser captures cover auth, dashboard, roadmap, lesson reading, data-lab reveal, quiz feedback, credits and fixed-provider status, product quality, and a 390px responsive dashboard with no console errors.

Seeded npm run e2e completed login → topic-specific roadmap → approval → no lesson prefetch → article lesson → completion → repeatable three-question quiz; the rich renderer browser smoke also passed code, equation, Mermaid, table, quote, references, and no legacy card selectors.
The earlier configurable provider flow was covered by a browser smoke test before provider access moved to a fixed backend configuration.

Live test with tema@synau.id and the saved Synau router provider: the router returned 404 only for forced tool_choice, while tools-based retry returned a valid roadmap. The backend now retries without forced tool_choice and parses JSON responses with trailing SSE DONE markers.

The saved provider generated a roadmap, then a lesson and a six-question quiz. One invalid lesson tool payload triggered the new Zod-guided repair pass and the corrected tool call validated successfully; no user course data was created by this probe.

43 checks passed with the earlier saved provider: auth/me/logout, provider settings, model discovery, connection test, roadmap, course CRUD state transitions, lazy article lesson generation/reopen/complete, inline citations and references, lesson/chapter/course quizzes, empty-answer rejection, repeatable attempts, activity, progress, and archive/reopen behavior. The temporary course was removed by explicit ID.

Headless browser passed login → roadmap generation → approval → no lesson prefetch → Open lesson → concurrency guard → flowing article → inline citation → references → completion → lesson quiz → submit. No page errors or HTTP 5xx responses were observed; evidence is quality/tema-provider-e2e.png and the temporary course was cleaned up.

Provider calls now default to a 120-second bounded timeout, retry tool calls without forced tool_choice on 400, 403, or 404 compatibility errors, parse JSON with trailing SSE DONE markers, perform two Zod-guided repair passes, reject incomplete quiz answers, and keep lesson generation lazy. The UI no longer duplicates quiz errors.
npm run build and npm run e2e passed on the final source. Seeded E2E evidence: login, roadmap, approval, no prefetch, lazy lesson, data-lab reveal, practice studio, completion, and repeatable quiz.

Every real provider generator request now sends thinking.type=disabled, including Zod repair retries. The saved Tema provider completed the full 39-check API contract run with roadmap, lesson, and all quiz scopes still passing.

Provider lesson output is now article-first: 2–5 sections of natural paragraphs, schema-checked source records, inline citation anchors, and an end references list. Optional supported components remain available for comparisons, examples, flows, scenarios, timelines, and code; malformed optional nodes cannot invalidate a valid article.

Practice and dataLab are no longer requested from the model; the server supplies safe defaults. Optional renderer nodes are capped at three in the provider tool contract, and an article-only result remains valid, reducing output size and avoiding unnecessary repair calls.

Lesson generation is single-flight per authenticated user across courses and tabs. Concurrent requests for the same lesson share one provider call; a different lesson receives 409 lesson_generation_in_progress with the active lesson details, and the UI explains that another lesson is being generated. Live API race, seeded E2E, and browser two-page QA all passed.

The per-user lesson-generation lock is persisted in Supabase with a five-minute crash-recovery lease. It closes the multi-process gap: another service process or harness cannot start a second lesson generation for the same user, while stale locks are cleaned automatically. Typecheck, production build, live API race, and browser two-page race checks all passed on the restarted server.

Live provider lessons now expose clickable inline source markers and a linked references list. Missing inline markers are repaired deterministically as further-reading links, while unknown citation IDs still fail Zod validation.

npm run build, npm run e2e, 43-check live API QA, and live provider browser QA all passed after the article-first refactor. The final browser capture shows natural paragraphs with optional supporting components and no lesson-generation 5xx.

Fixed every tool-based generator request to send stream:false and Accept: application/json. Live Synau calls for roadmap, lazy lesson, and lesson/chapter/course quizzes all returned successfully and produced fresh successful usage rows in the 9router telemetry store with prompt, completion, and cost values; the temporary course was removed.

Removed the alternate account provider path from the UI, callback route, client header forwarding, generator backend, model discovery, database activation path, environment template, and package dependencies. Provider credentials now live only in backend environment configuration; the new credit/browser smoke, health check, and removed-callback 404 check all passed.

Moved provider identity, base URL, model, and API key to backend environment configuration. A live roadmap, lazy lesson, repeatable quizzes, and browser workflow passed with Sumopod deepseek-v4-flash; the browser received no provider key and the fixed provider cannot be changed through the UI.

Added backend wallet, append-only ledger, generation holds with unused-credit refunds, LLM usage records for input/cached/output/total tokens, and a seeded 10,000-credit demo grant. The live API run settled seven successful usage rows and moved the demo balance from 9,700 to 7,200 credits without a negative balance.

Integrated @theyahia/midtrans-mcp for Snap token creation and status lookup, added signed/idempotent notification handling, and verified a synthetic settlement credits a top-up exactly once. The supplied key pair was rejected with HTTP 401 in both sandbox and production, so the real Snap checkout still needs corrected Midtrans credentials.

Missing provider configuration now defaults to the fixed Sumopod identity instead of silently switching to another provider; the MCP subprocess receives only required Midtrans environment values. Typecheck, production build, and credits browser smoke passed.

Each library card now has a restrained three-dot menu with Rename path and Delete course actions. Rename uses a validated PATCH and preserves course content/progress; delete uses a server-side cascade with generation-lock protection and a second confirmation dialog. Temporary-database browser E2E passed rename, cancel-delete, and confirmed-delete alongside the complete learner workflow.

Roadmap, lesson, and quiz generators now each reserve and settle exactly 1 credit. Provider retries remain inside one billing scope; invalid, failed, timed-out, and stale reservations are refunded. Live Sumopod QA passed six successful generators with six credit charges, and the demo account received an idempotent additional 10,000-credit development top-up.

Settings now exposes Rp15.000, Rp30.000, Rp50.000, and Rp100.000 packages with totals 1.500, 3.010, 5.025, and 10.050 credits; bonuses are 0, 10, 25, and 50. New accounts receive exactly 100 free credits through an idempotent backend ledger grant. Browser smoke passed package rendering and repeated balance reads.

Replaced password sign-in and registration with six-digit email verification. Sign up collects First Name, Last Name, username, and email; sign in accepts email or username. Codes are hashed, expire after ten minutes, allow five attempts, are single-use, and enforce resend cooldown. SMTP delivery uses a proper HTML/text template; local console delivery is explicit development fallback. The demo account accepts 020599. Auth unit smoke and temporary-database browser E2E passed, and legacy password routes return 404.

Removed the learner-facing top navigation, moved profile/settings/library/credits links into the profile menu, surfaced the live credit balance beside the profile, kept /quality directly accessible but hidden from navigation, capped the dashboard library at six recent cards, and added a full /library route. The browser UI shell smoke passed with seven temporary paths, exact six-card dashboard rendering, profile-to-credits navigation, direct quality access, and full-library rendering; fixtures were deleted afterward.

Applied the Zod-aligned Supabase schema with RLS, server-only RPCs, Supabase Auth profile mapping, and all application data migrated. The runtime now requires Supabase, removes the native local database dependency, and passes health, publishable/Auth connectivity, REST privilege boundary, and main port 8787 checks.

latestResults.area: Supabase remote learner and billing QA
latestResults.result: Remote deterministic browser/API QA passed roadmap approval, lazy lesson, article renderer, practice, completion, repeatable lesson/chapter/course quiz paths, progress, archive guard, library manager, and cleanup. A bounded live Sumopod probe then passed roadmap, lesson, and quiz with input/cached/output/total token usage recorded, exactly one credit settled per generator, and a 3-credit balance delta.

Supabase email OTP was removed from the active runtime after the auth policy changed to Google-only. The retired email-code endpoints return an explicit 410 response and no local auth harness remains.

Supabase mode now exposes only Google sign-in. The browser resumes the Supabase OAuth session, the backend verifies the Google identity server-side, links a migrated profile by verified email when safe, and requests First Name, Last Name, and username only for a new Synau profile. Email-code endpoints return google_auth_only, non-Google Supabase tokens are rejected, and the setup command is npm run auth:configure-google. Hosted provider credentials and redirect URL configuration remain external setup steps.

Fixed the first-login completion response to map backend user fields from snake_case to the public camelCase Zod contract before sending JSON. The observed user profile and 100 welcome credits were already persisted; retrying the same OAuth session is idempotent and now completes instead of showing a generic 503.

Disabled Midtrans calls and webhook with explicit midtrans_disabled responses; payment packages remain locked mockups. Added a random database-only 1,500-credit reviewer token, one redemption per account, local and Supabase schema support, and an in-app redeem field above the locked packages. Local safety test passed first redemption at 1,500 and repeated redemption at zero additional credits.

Main now uses short-lived GET caching with in-flight deduplication, event-driven credit refreshes, lazy route chunks, duplicate completion/quiz guards, and batched Supabase course-list reads that omit lesson material. The main checkout typecheck/build passed; the Supabase browser smoke verified one courses read, one credits read, cache-hot route clicks, single refreshes after expiry, and one credit refresh after roadmap generation.

Removed the local database runtime, seed/migration fallback, local auth-code harness, native database dependencies, and local QA branches. Server startup now fails clearly when Supabase is unavailable; generator billing, lesson locks, course CRUD, progress, quizzes, and credits all use Supabase paths.

New lesson output is a natural article stream. A real browser fixture rendered a code snippet, KaTeX equation, Mermaid SVG diagram, accessible table, quote, key takeaway, and references in one flowing lesson; no practice, comparison, data-lab, reflection, or about-this-material card surface remained.

GeneratedQuizSchema and the provider tool contract require exactly three questions: two kind=article with article anchors from supplied material and one kind=challenge for relevant transfer. The browser displayed the labels From the article, From the article, and Challenge, while public responses kept answer keys private.

Roadmap, lesson, and quiz calls each create one billing scope and reserve one credit. Repair retries and optional lesson renderers stay inside the same scope; successful work settles exactly one credit and failed or stale work refunds it. Live provider API QA settled six successful generators with a six-credit balance delta, and the failed malformed attempt refunded its hold.

Production-build API QA passed roadmap, lazy lesson, lesson quiz repeat, chapter quiz, course quiz, completion, archive guard, progress endpoint, public answer-key protection, and logout. Every quiz returned exactly two article questions followed by one challenge. Production-build browser QA also passed the same learner workflow with no HTTP 5xx or page errors; evidence is quality/tema-provider-e2e.png.

The provider QA loop exposed oversized chapter context, malformed quiz output, and repeated answer positions. Quiz prompts now compact material and memory, bound anchors/options/explanations, deterministic fallback questions use article context, and the backend reorders options without changing correct answers. The rerun passed API and browser QA.

The remote CRUD harness passed list, create, detail, rename, complete, and delete against the running main server. Each mutation used exactly one operation RPC query; list/detail omitted lesson material; completion returned updated progress; observed round trips were about 0.13–0.53s with one auth-boundary query at most.

The remote deterministic Supabase browser harness passed one dashboard courses request, one credits request, zero requests for cache-hot Credits/Library clicks, one courses plus one credits refresh after expiry, and one roadmap request plus one credit refresh after generation. Latest p95 API timings were 679ms on first dashboard load, 447ms after expiry, and 157ms for the deterministic roadmap mutation; the remote server recorded at most two Supabase queries per request.

Seeded browser E2E, the full provider-shaped API harness, UI shell smoke, typecheck, and production build passed after the refactor. The API harness covered auth, roadmap, lazy lesson, concurrent lesson lock, article rendering contract, lesson/chapter/course quizzes, repeatable attempts, completion, archive guard, progress, and logout. Demo-mode billing was explicitly excluded; live-provider billing assertions remain strict.

The live personal-branding provider run produced a two-sentence overview, a distinct 65-word Indonesian opening, a four-section article, natural inline references, and a Mermaid diagram for the inventory framework. The browser capture quality/prompt-personal-branding.png showed no legacy lesson cards and no page or HTTP errors.

Strict lesson Zod validation remains in place while the backend normalizes safe aliases such as text on code, equation, Mermaid, paragraph, and quote blocks and removes unsupported block fields. This avoids a repair call for semantically equivalent provider output; typecheck and production build passed, followed by the live browser workflow.

The deterministic seeded browser workflow still passed login, roadmap approval, true lazy lesson generation, the new two-sentence/45-word intro assertions, article-only rendering with no legacy cards, completion, and repeatable quiz flow. Evidence is quality/e2e-final.png.
